value.definition: Feedback observes, compares governing conditions, diagnoses material discrepancy, selects an authorised response, acts and observes again. Homeostasis is correction towards required conditions without a convergence or adequacy guarantee. Bugs are observed or suspected discrepancies within feature/change work and its existing intake and delivery mechanism. Diagnosis distinguishes defective realisation, inadequate requirement or design, inaccurate predictive model and insufficient observation; severity describes consequence while priority orders response.

grounding.quote:
Diagnosis distinguishes four causes: a defective realisation, an
inadequate governing requirement or design, an inaccurate predictive
model, and insufficient observation.

value.label: Feedback, diagnosis and bug work

value.definition: Exact, self-reconstructing execution intake naming the governed outcome, admitted prerequisite or experiment; subject, basis and acquirable inputs; evaluation and result algebra; affected relations and invariants; accepted transformation admissions; computational dispositions; construction and assessment authorities and grant; actor envelopes; invalidation and re-entry conditions; and, for a cost claim, allowance and spend measurement.

grounding.quote:
A step is activated from an intake sufficient to reconstruct its governing
relations without conversation history, commentary or a prior actor's memory
(P0, actor-change premise). The intake names:

value.label: Intake

value.definition: Smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable of delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing relation. It need not match a function, file, module, ticket field or design document. This cone is the context procedure's seed set Z, distinct in use from construction's destination predicate Z; context is its projection.

grounding.quote:
The execution unit is the smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable
of delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing
relation. It need not coincide with one function, file, module, ticket
field or design document (P0, P4b; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD
#bounded-causal-construction). A seam whose far side can causally affect,
or be affected by, the action is inside the cone unless the basis
establishes that it cannot participate. Unrelated incompleteness outside
the cone is recorded as repricing input and does not block the bounded
claim. The cone is the seed set Z of §2; the context is its projection.

value.label: Execution unit

value.definition: Step contract with at least drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded states. Drafting and admitting are separate relations even in one invocation; that distinction implies no separate turn, carrier or ceremony. An admitted contract names one durable result and evidence surface.

grounding.quote:
Drafting a step's contract and admitting it are distinct relations, even
inside one invocation that drafts, validates, admits and executes; no
separate turn, carrier or approval ceremony is implied by the distinction.
A contract carries at minimum the states drafted, admitted, rejected and
superseded ([TICKETS §5](TICKETS.md#execution-contract-admission)).

value.label: Execution contract and admission

value.definition: Basis-bound evaluation of the predicate that a frame obligation applies to the exact subject, owned by the evaluation and scope declarations. Exclusion is the obligation's state following falsified applicability, not a result of that obligation.

grounding.quote:
The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame
obligations apply to the exact subject. Their declared predicates are
evaluated from sufficient basis-bound facts: a true predicate requires the
applicable evaluation and its result; a false predicate excludes only that
obligation, under its cited authority; a missing or ambiguous premise
leaves applicability unresolved, not false.

value.label: Applicability and exclusion

value.definition: Candidate plus step-produced facts: judgments and evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance and one construction-availability stop state. The actor's internal path is neither output nor governed.

grounding.quote:
The step's output is a candidate plus its step-produced facts: judgments with
their evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance, and
one stop state, a value of construction availability (§3). The actor's
internal path is not part of the output
and is not governed (FOUNDATIONS §2, work boundary; provenance
[Probabilistic Work Boundary](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#probabilistic-work-boundary)).

value.label: Step output

value.definition: Allocation of task responsibilities and information exchanges to frames across the task's work; activation binds actors to frames. The active frame configuration is the portion used for one evaluation or decision. Reconfiguration is any change of allocation during work, including actors redistributing work.

grounding.quote:
A configuration allocates a task's responsibilities and information
exchanges to frames; activation binds an actor to each frame (§2). It
spans the task's work. The active frame configuration of
[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects) is the part of it used for
one evaluation or decision (P0, P6).

value.label: Configuration and reconfiguration

conditions: The executive baseline profile is selected.
value.definition: Illustrative, nondefault configuration separating bounded change from delivery across tasks: Worker, specialised as Writer for documents and records, constructs; Reviewer assesses; Executive keeps the longer-term outcome, selects work and disposes within its grant while mutating nothing. The profile owns its frames, grants, limits, prohibitions and explanation.

grounding.quote:
Worker frame, specialised as Writer for documents and records, constructs;
a Reviewer frame assesses; an Executive frame keeps the longer-term
outcome, selects the next work and disposes within its decision grant, and
mutates nothing. That profile owns its frames, their grants, limits and
prohibitions, and its explanation; they apply where it is selected. It is
not the method's default. A configuration with other frames, names or
topology is evaluated as Evaluation of a configuration above states.

value.label: Executive configuration example

value.definition: Roles are configuration-allocated relations over steps, not actor kinds or a fixed inventory. Where those operations exist, constructor owns implementation and self-review, assessor independently evaluates a frozen candidate, and decision owner disposes. Other responsibilities may be allocated.

grounding.quote:
Roles are relations over steps that a configuration allocates
(Configuration above), not kinds of actor and not a fixed inventory.
Where a configuration's operations include construction, assessment or
disposition, this member names the responsibility for each: a
constructor owns the bounded implementation and its self-review; an
assessor evaluates a frozen candidate independently; a decision owner
disposes. A configuration may allocate other responsibilities.

value.label: Roles and delegation

value.definition: Declared procedure over intake seed set Z, material dependency family R and actor envelope B: compute finite unique material closure on an exact basis; project with explicit seams; test envelope fit; acquire declared inputs by exact identity. Here seed Z comprises subject, outcome and affected relations, not the destination predicate's use of Z.

grounding.quote:
Given a seed set Z (the subject, outcome and affected relations named in the
intake), a relation family R (the dependency relations whose change can
alter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency or authority), and
the actor's envelope B:

value.label: Context construction under an envelope

value.definition: Acquisition is read-only observation of the frame, subject and declared inputs permitted by intake, not admission or an additional actor stage. A derived surface copies, projects or compresses owning sources, names them and owns no determination; a current a_c task constraint surface is one such surface.

grounding.quote:
Acquisition. Acquisition is the read-only observation of the material a
step needs (its frame, its subject and its declared inputs) within the
inputs its intake permits it to acquire (§1 Intake). It is not an admission and not a further
actor stage; effectful work still needs its admitted contract (§1
Admission), and acquiring material grants no role, operation or decision
([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
creates no authority). A derived surface is material derived from owning
sources by copying, projection or compression, such as a projected frame
for a task; it names its sources and owns no determination. Where a
current interpretation of the subject in `a_c` exists, the constraint
surface it yields for the task is such a derived surface, under the
conditions of
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §9 Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).

value.label: Acquisition and derived surfaces

value.definition: Prompt is rendered contract over typed authority, not source law. It projects current authority references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations and fallback conditions needed by the step.

grounding.quote:
Prompt construction. A prompt is rendered contract over typed authority;
it is not source law. Prompt text must project the current authority
references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations and
fallback conditions the step needs.

value.label: Prompt construction

value.definition: Source-identity currentness of a derived surface for a selected basis, applicable to any method and carrier. Currentness, fidelity, question-specific sufficiency and source ownership are separate matters.

grounding.quote:
This subsection owns when a derived surface (Acquisition above) is current
and when it is stale, for any method and any carrier (P3, P5, P6):

value.label: Staleness of derived surfaces

value.definition: Five result refinements with distinct questions and mapping predicates: admission/activation—lawfully admitted and activated on exact subject and basis; construction availability—a candidate is available; disposition—candidate accepted at declared boundary; ambiguity outcome—declared ambiguity resolved on exact basis; effects—intended effect occurred.

grounding.quote:
| admission and activation | may the step begin | the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis |
| construction availability | did the step yield its output | a candidate is available |
| disposition | what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate | the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary |
| ambiguity outcome | what happened to a declared ambiguity | the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis |
| effects | did an intended external effect occur | the intended effect occurred |

value.label: Core result refinements

value.definition: Pre-step result domain for lawful admission and activation on exact subject and basis. Values named here are activated, admission_refused(authority), admission_refused(basis), closure_unresolved, out_of_frame and activation_refusal with its cause. REFERENCE_FRAME owns the frame activate refinement and its causes and core mappings.

grounding.quote:
A step exists only after its contract is admitted (§1, Admission) and its
frame is activated on the exact subject and basis (§2). The outcomes of
admission and of context construction are owned here; each maps for the
predicate "the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact
subject and basis", and its cause selects its value (P5, P6; RF-005 for
the basis causes). The outcomes of frame activation are the `activate`
refinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),
which owns their causes, their predicate and their core values. Because
this predicate requires activation, a refused activation decides it with
the value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives; the table names those outcomes and
maps none of them again:

value.label: Admission and activation outcomes

conditions: Lawful activation has occurred.
value.definition: Result domain deciding whether the step's output exists. Output remains a candidate until evaluated: the constructed subject for a constructing step or closed results for an assessing step. Values are candidate_ready, refused, incomplete, re_entry_requested(authority) and re_entry_requested(basis).

grounding.quote:
A step's output is a candidate until evaluated (FOUNDATIONS §3, P0): the
constructed subject of a constructing step, or the closed results of an
assessing step. Construction availability records whether that output
exists (P5, P6; provenance
[work result](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#work-result)):

value.label: Construction availability

conditions: An assessed candidate is presented to its decision owner.
value.definition: Owner's acceptance result at a declared boundary, distinct from candidate availability, assessment and an assessor's recommendation. Four semantic dispositions are accept, local_repair, re_enter and reject.

grounding.quote:
The decision owner disposes an assessed candidate with one of four
semantic dispositions (§1, Roles and delegation; P6, P5; provenance rc.2
SPEC_METHOD #proportional-disposition). An assessor may recommend one; the
recommendation is evidence for the decision owner, never a disposition
([EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results)). The disposition is the
acceptance result: it consumes the candidate's availability and assessment
results and stays separate from both (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results). Each maps
to the core for the predicate "the candidate is accepted at its declared
boundary":

value.label: Semantic disposition

conditions: There is a declared ambiguity.
value.definition: Recorded result domain for whether that ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis: resolved, carried, escalated or blocked.

grounding.quote:
A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
outcome is recorded either way (§4, which also names the hard stops;
[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
applies this to the method's chain of authority surfaces). Each outcome
maps to the core for the predicate "the declared ambiguity is resolved on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

value.label: Ambiguity outcome

conditions: A step has an intended external effect.
value.definition: Evidence-based result for whether the effect's declared outcome is attained: completed, not_effected or completion_unknown. Whether the effect has ended is a separate question; uncertain completion includes completion_unknown and not_effected with unestablished end.

grounding.quote:
An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
premise, P6):

value.label: External-effect outcome and end

value.definition: Total handling declares next moves for all admitted condition classes, including unknown. Hard stops are nonoptional conditions regardless of ambiguity risk appetite. Reconfiguration selects a cause-responsive change after out_of_frame, invalid_basis, repeated indeterminate or incompatible results.

grounding.quote:
Next moves after any non-satisfied result are named in advance: continue
within the current contract when supported; refine; recover; yield; re-enter
the owning relation; terminate. Each admitted condition class has a declared
next move, including an explicit unknown class. Total handling does not
claim that every external condition is recognised, that an invoked provider
terminates, or that every request can be completed. A hanging external call,
an unsatisfiable demand and a lost post-effect response are three different
cases and none is solved by adding a value to the algebra.

value.label: Totality, hard stops and reconfiguration

value.definition: Refinement decomposes an outer transformation T: A → X into steps; rewrite replaces a representation, step or composite with another claimed to retain meaning. A licensing law is a subject-owner-declared permission such as associativity, commutativity or equivalence. Exact steps preserve declared meaning; approximate steps require an adequacy relation and a composite end-to-end bound.

grounding.quote:
Preservation and licensing. A refinement step decomposes a transformation
into steps, as above. A rewrite step replaces a representation, a step or
a composite by another that is claimed to keep its meaning, for example
by partitioning, regrouping, reordering, merging or substituting parts.
Each refinement layer, the steps that refine one transformation, states
what it preserves of the layer above, the transformation it refines, and
discharges that obligation (P4a, P6). A refinement or rewrite step is
admissible only under the laws declared for its subject. Its licensing law is the declared
law that permits it, such as an associativity, commutativity or
equivalence law that the subject's owner declares for the subject.

value.label: Refinement, rewriting and approximation

conditions: A material transition is proposed.
value.definition: Each admission owner's independent derivation and validation of the complete enclosing relation from authoritative inputs, followed by one semantic commit of the complete transition on an exact basis, or none.

grounding.quote:
For a material transition, each admission owner is independently
responsible for deriving and validating the complete enclosing relation
from authoritative inputs (P4b, P6; provenance
[UP-021](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#complete-enclosing-relation-admission-stdo-up-021)).
The relation contains every participant and equality join whose identity,
validity, authority, currentness or transition can affect or be affected by
admission; each crossing seam includes its relevant far side or
authoritatively establishes that the far side cannot participate. Caller or
owner assertions of completeness, validity, prior admission or authority do
not establish truth.

value.label: Complete enclosing-relation admission

conditions: For every admission owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design.
value.definition: Standing qualification of enclosing-relation admission against the supported input, state and operating or threat model. Excluded threats alone create neither acceptance predicates nor defensive-work requirements; scope expansion returns to its owner, while supported malformed inputs, stale state and effect boundaries retain checks.

grounding.quote:
Qualification of the admission law is instantiated for every admission
owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design (P6; provenance
rc.2 SPEC_METHOD #standing-structural-qualification). Case applicability
follows the supported input, state and operating or threat model. An
excluded threat alone cannot create an acceptance predicate or require
defensive work; a proposed scope expansion returns to its owning authority.
Supported malformed inputs, stale state and effect boundaries retain their
required checks:

value.label: Standing structural qualification

value.definition: Persistent object comprising workspace, governing basis, applicable closed results and judgments with invalidators, residuals and known external-effect uncertainty. Resumption re-enters the same method on current material state, possibly with another actor; checkpointing, resumption and progress accounting are generic procedures with no prescribed carrier.

grounding.quote:
Work state is the tuple of: the current persistent workspace; the governing
basis; the applicable closed results and judgments with their invalidators;
the residuals; and the known uncertainty over external effects. It is an
object (P3); its carrier (files, an event stream, another admitted owner) is
a profile or realisation choice. Resumption, checkpointing and the
progress account of this section are generic procedures
([SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding)): they require
no particular carrier (P1, P6).

value.label: Work state, resumption and checkpoint

value.definition: Semantic categories: progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome; prerequisite work names the obligation enabled; preservation and repeated proof are evidence rather than new progress; rejected or superseded construction is churn; discovery of hidden distance revises the forecast rather than constituting negative progress. These are not a numeric algorithm.

grounding.quote:
Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome;
prerequisite work names the obligation it enables; preservation and
repeated proof are evidence, not new progress; rejected or superseded
construction is churn; discovering previously hidden distance revises the
forecast and is not negative progress. Paperwork, code volume, test count,
commit count and review count are not progress by themselves. These are
semantic categories, not a numeric progress algorithm; a consumer may
derive its own progress and churn projections from them (P2).

value.label: Progress, prerequisite work, evidence, churn and forecast revision

value.definition: The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations. Their current material state is the continuing truth surface for what the work has and has not done; work state preserves applicable valid work and outstanding obligations.

grounding.quote:
The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations and
are the continuing truth surface of the work: the surface whose current
material state decides what the work has and has not done.

value.label: Workspace truth surface

value.definition: An actor's context is a bounded projection and revisable account of work state, disposable because closed results and needed step-produced facts are recorded before return. It is never another truth surface. Later intake reconstructs governing relations without a predecessor's private context.

grounding.quote:
An account is
never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without
it

value.label: Actor account

value.definition: Proportionality relates material semantic ambiguity removed to effective reasoning complexity introduced. Complexity includes independent concepts and authority surfaces, cross-document joins, exceptions, branching, states, transitions, reconciled duplicates and decision detail; it is not line count, artifact count or context-window size. A detailed model may be proportional and a short extra truth surface disproportionate.

grounding.quote:
Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and
effective reasoning complexity introduced. A method obligation is
proportional when its contraction of the admissible interpretation space
justifies the additional concepts, relations, projections and evidence an
actor must hold together to reach a correct decision

value.label: Proportionality and effective reasoning complexity

conditions: A cost claim is the governed question.
value.definition: Selected cost is an activation's declared allowance and reported spend, measured under a selected execution binding or explicitly unmeasured. Material startup, framework processing, external computation, transport and assurance are separate components. Transferred-context cost includes every delegated actor, not merely coordinator traffic or report volume.

grounding.quote:
Cost is selected, not universal. Where a cost claim is the governed
question, the activation declares its allowance and reports its spend,
measured under the selected execution binding or recorded as unmeasured

value.label: Selected cost claim

value.definition: A resource limit bounds context, attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or machine resources consumed by an activation. This subsection owns the generic declaration, measurement and exhaustion law but sets no values; the selected execution binding supplies values and measurable units and boundaries.

grounding.quote:
A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value

value.label: Declared resource limit

value.definition: A closed result identifies its frame, activation, subject, basis, evaluation, actor, evidence, verdict, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions. It supports handoff without private working context while retaining validity and independence conditions.

grounding.quote:
A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
uncertainty and the invalidation conditions

value.label: Closed result

value.definition: Result invalidation has exactly three kinds: a material subject or relied-on input change, including admissible evidence capable of changing the result's value; change to any bound basis coordinate; and occurrence of an observation explicitly declared to revise the result or judgment. Affectedness is expressed as dependencies D*(t) meeting impact cover I(Δ). Invalidation withdraws direct reliance without deciding the underlying claim's truth.

grounding.quote:
- a changed basis: a change to any coordinate of the basis the result
  binds (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis);
- a declared revising observation: an observation that the result or
  judgment itself names as one that would revise it, once it occurs.

value.label: Three kinds of result invalidation

value.definition: Transition evidence is a consumer-chosen read model identifying the exact candidate, affected relations, changed realisation paths, authority paths added or removed, retained and open seams, focused proof, required integration proof and explicit non-changes. If an assessor was activated it includes the recommendation, with the decision owner's disposition beside it once made.

grounding.quote:
Transition evidence is a read
model; it does not become specification, design or admission authority

value.label: Transition evidence

value.definition: The source-disposition register states predecessor conservation, successor loci, new rules and pending proposals. It places UP-020 across activation, disposition, restart and transition evidence; UP-018 reconstruction in Intake and DESIGN_MODULE; probabilistic work commitments in FOUNDATIONS; RF engagement across activation and reuse; AC-010/011 and RF context laws in their owning successors; RF-012/AC-007 result algebra and result conjunction in FOUNDATIONS; ticket admission in ACTIVATION with TICKETS disposing its rows; ambiguity outcomes and hard stops in ACTIVATION with SPEC_METHOD ownership; general typed refinement in ACTIVATION while ODD 11.8 remains profile-specific; UP-017 in DESIGN_MODULE; UP-021 and ten standing-qualification forms in ACTIVATION §4; proportionality and cost in ACTIVATION, delivery in SPEC_METHOD and UP-005/019 in DESIGN_MODULE; generic result reuse in ACTIVATION and ticket continuity in TICKETS. The register calls workspace/account, foundation tables, transitions, configuration, effects, derived-surface staleness, parts of refinement, context acquisition/measurement, allowance and generic resource-limit rules new. These are reported source claims, not verified conservation judgments.

grounding.quote: a table decides nothing and names the rule that states each consequence.

| Return A Closed Result | conserved; §7, which names the invalidators once as three kinds (material input change, with newly acquired or changed material evidence, from TICKET judgment continuity; changed basis; declared revising observation) and requires a domain trigger to be stated as an instance of one of them (new, with its purpose stated there) |

value.label: ACTIVATION predecessor-disposition register

value.definition: ASSURANCE is a tier-2 document owning verification layers, testing taxonomy and its two proof authorities, portability, test authority, scenario bundles, installed proof, significant paths, testing frames, combinatorial value, path/debt erasure, evidence composition, subject acquisition, localisation and interface integration. It consumes tier-1 laws without redefining them. SPEC_METHOD supplies chain/change classes and PRODUCT_DEFINITION project bindings. It does not pre-empt design-profile module proof or TICKETS test-case authority and does not depend on the tier-3 Executive profile. rc.2 and baseline anchors are provenance only; received predecessor rules are stated to be restated for standalone use.

grounding.quote: reuse); adds no definition to tier 1.

both are provenance only. Under the standalone successor requirement every
predecessor row received here is restated in full in this text, and
nothing here depends on that cut to be applied.

value.label: ASSURANCE document role

value.definition: Requirements preserve invariant truth and ask what must be true; design preserves structural choice and asks how it is realised; scenarios preserve operational meaning and ask whether the realised system can do the claimed thing. Scenarios are the product-owner layer of concrete end-to-end use cases validating intent through realised behaviour, including whether a reusable unit can actually be built and applied twice.

grounding.quote:
| Requirements | invariant truth | what must be true? |
| Design | structural choice | how is that truth realised? |
| Scenarios | operational meaning | can the realised system actually do the claimed thing? |

value.label: Requirements, design and scenario verification layers

conditions: The applicable instance premises hold; commitments alone do not supply them.
value.definition: F14 accounts for assurance and testing laws in §§1–16; §17 records dispositions and decides nothing. Its instance premises are a runnable/observable product in source and runnable forms, composition of modules/interfaces/owners along causal paths, user outcomes through supported surfaces, possible external workers/transports/fixtures and possibly design-governed module boundaries. Fourteen rows distinguish commitment-supported consequences from member-owned domain or policy choices and other owners. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are marked independent; P5 is derived from P0/P6 with an open-world premise and P4b from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts. The family records proof authorities, sandbox modes, fixture alternatives, scenario/path categories, installed-proof preference, four testing frames, path mutation policy, value coordinates, owner-issued subjects, four localisation forms, interface claims, module proof and lifecycle confirmation.

grounding.quote:
decides what evidence proves a claim about a realised product and how
that evidence is organised. Its instance premises, which the commitments
do not supply, are named in the rows as follows: runnable product, a
product's realisation can be executed or observed, in a source form and in
a deployed, installed or otherwise runnable form, to produce evidence;

value.label: F14 assurance and testing foundation-to-law family

value.definition: Within urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance, Product-level proof authority has two primary sources independent of execution breadth: design/module conformance and UAT/acceptance. Conformance derives from governing design, module ownership, declared carrier inventory or equivalent, structural diagrams where present and local fail-closed law; unit tests belong here, as may integration/negative/fail-closed tests targeting a designed boundary. Acceptance derives from requirements, acceptance criteria, scenarios/use cases and Product release/qualification claims. The shared context does not merge the design profile's module-proof authority with Product authority.

grounding.quote:
Authority source is not execution breadth. A test may be small or broad,
fast or slow, deterministic or live, and still derives from one of two
primary authorities (P6, P1):

1. design or module conformance tests; and
2. UAT, or acceptance, tests.

value.label: Two proof-authority sources

value.definition: Sandbox UAT exercises a deployed, installed or otherwise runnable composed Product through declared application, public, runtime or control surfaces using a requirement-sourced scenario or acceptance case. Harnessed mode uses deterministic, fake, recorded or injected worker/result surfaces for reproducible composition, orchestration, control, projection, archive and scenario wiring. Live mode crosses a real configured external worker, tool, agent, service or probabilistic transport and returns evidence through declared result, evaluation, provenance and projection surfaces.

grounding.quote:
- harnessed sandbox UAT exercises the full composed product path with a
  deterministic, fake, recorded or injected worker or result surface; and
- live sandbox UAT exercises the full composed product path with a real
  configured worker, tool, agent, service or other external probabilistic
  transport where the product depends on that live boundary.

value.label: Harnessed and live sandbox UAT

value.definition: Fixture and proof portability makes required closure lanes reproducible from a declared source boundary. External project evidence is carried by a minimal checked-in fixture, a manifest naming external source/version/acquisition or binding rule, or classification outside required semantic closure.

grounding.quote:
- a minimal fixture is checked into the source boundary;
- a fixture manifest declares the external source, version and
  acquisition or binding rule; or
- the test is classified as harnessed sandbox, live sandbox, reference
  comparison or optional local evidence rather than required semantic
  closure.

value.label: Fixture and proof portability

value.definition: Written traceable test-case authority for a live requirement may contain scenario bundles, ordered sequences, negative/control cases and other evidence cases appropriate to the truth claimed. Each expected result carries assertion provenance: owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation, shared dependencies and whether its predicate is the obligation, a necessary condition or part of a sufficient conjunction.

grounding.quote:
Written authority includes the assertion
provenance of each expected result: the owning obligation, its
interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies, and
whether the asserted predicate is the obligation, a necessary condition of
it or part of a sufficient conjunction

value.label: Written test-case authority

value.definition: A scenario bundle exposes the feature/use-case boundary, ordered test-case sequence and expected outcomes at significant steps. Scenarios make operational meaning inspectable and constrain intent/design by naming real boundaries, sequences, actors, controls and outcomes; the source calls them the best source for identifying significant code and control paths.

grounding.quote:
A scenario bundle shows the feature or use-case boundary being exercised,
the test-case sequence that proves it, and the outcomes expected at each
significant step. It is the layer that makes operational meaning
inspectable

value.label: Scenario bundle

conditions: The system has an installable or runnable development form.
value.definition: Installed-dev proof is the decisive lane against an installed development version treated as an independent project or external target, rather than source-tree-only proof.

grounding.quote:
Where a system has an installable or runnable development form, the
decisive proving lane runs against an installed development version as if
it were an independent project or an externalised target, not only against
the source tree in place

value.label: Installed development proof

value.definition: Significant paths are the meaningful paths of the claimed behaviour. Usually, where relevant, they include success, fail-closed/rejection, boundary/control, integration/dispatch/transport and recovery/retry/replay. Exhaustive proof means intentional proof of named meaningful paths, not every branch in every file.
value.label: Significant behaviour paths

value.definition: The named ASSURANCE section grouping the Product testing frame set; this heading alone supplies no activation or frame declaration.

grounding.quote: ## 7. Product testing frame set

value.label: Product testing frame set section

value.definition: A testing frame executes or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim using an explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification condition. An authoritative Product path is the ordinary causal composition from supported entry through exact selected interfaces, owners, transitions, effects, persistence and recovery to the required outcome projection. Material combinatorial complexity is the claim-relative population of independent dimensions/interactions capable of changing outcomes, invariants, authority paths or failures; module laws and public module contracts belong at unit altitude, whereas cross-participant/Product/persistence/configuration/user-role combinations belong at broader congruent frames.

grounding.quote:
A testing frame is a frame (REFERENCE_FRAME §1) whose evaluation executes
or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim through an
explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification
condition.

Material combinatorial complexity is the claim-relative population of
independent dimensions and interactions whose combinations can change an
outcome, violate an invariant, select another authority path or expose a

value.label: Testing frame, authoritative path and material combinations

conditions: The governing frame configuration or admitted work authority selects testing frames for a Product promotion, closure or release-assurance claim.
value.definition: A claim-relative frame configuration ordinarily assigns user outcomes to user acceptance, complete runnable causal paths to end-to-end, material composition boundaries and interactions to integration, and one module-owned law to unit. This is evidence assignment, not a role/stage/authority hierarchy or decomposition of frames. Placement makes laws available without adopting or activating them; ACTIVATION applicability decides activation.

grounding.quote:
Placement in this member makes the
set, and the law of §8 to §13 that serves it, available; it adopts nothing,
and each activation is decided by ACTIVATION §1 (Applicability). The kind
of runner does not select the frame; the evaluated claim, subject, path,
population, oracle and falsification boundary do

value.label: Claim-relative testing frame configuration

conditions: Selected for an exact user-outcome claim.
value.definition: User acceptance asks whether a declared user with admitted capability/information can obtain the exact Product-defined outcome through the ordinary supported surface. It binds the exact runnable Product; current Product, requirement, UX, identity, policy and acceptance authority; user role/environment and harnessed/live mode. Its manifold includes goals, entries, permissions, inputs, configuration, ordinary dependencies, declared substitutions, visible states/outputs, refusals, recovery and acceptance interval. Coordinates distinguish Product/artifact/install, role/capability, configuration/dependencies/mode, data/workspace/invocation/time/outcome/scenario. Evidence includes supported requests/responses, projections, claimed durable effects, refusals/recovery, scenario and subject/dependency identity. Its envelope supports acting and perceiving as that user and detecting hidden assistance.

grounding.quote: | evaluation family | Can a declared user, with the user's admitted capability and information, obtain the exact Product-defined outcome through the supported ordinary Product surface? |

value.label: User-acceptance frame

conditions: Selected for an exact complete runnable causal-path claim.
value.definition: End-to-end evaluation binds the exact runnable Product, composition design, supported entry, selected owners/dependencies, ordinary runtime configuration and Product claim. It follows every material interface, owner, transition, effect, persistence, continuation, recovery and projection boundary, including competing paths. Coordinates include artifact/installed tree, entry/operation, selected definition/owner, path/edges, process/event prefix/state, configuration/dependency/result/replay/scenario. Evidence is supported invocation, observed semantic path/authority edges, owner receipts, durable events, transitions/outputs, claimed replay/reconstruction, installed identity and negative-path observations. Its envelope permits observing the complete unchanged path, distinguishing rivals and reproducing material state/failure relations.

grounding.quote: | evaluation family | Does the exact Product subject realise the claimed outcome through the complete authoritative Product path, including every material interface, owner, state transition, effect, persistence, continuation, recovery and projection boundary? |

value.label: End-to-end frame

conditions: Selected for one declared material composition boundary.
value.definition: Integration evaluates actual participants' joint contract over outcome-changing state, authority, configuration, timing, failure and recovery combinations. It binds exact interface/composition declaration, actual implementations or exact substitutes admitted by the bounded claim, Product/requirement/design law and interaction population. Both boundary sides, shared carriers, pre/postconditions, ownership, ordering, translation and competitors are material. Coordinates distinguish participant/version, interface/carrier revision, state/configuration/dependency, case/input/output/failure/evidence. Evidence includes exchanges, admitted carriers, transitions, verdicts, failures/retries/recovery, combinations and identities; the envelope permits observing the real seam, detecting substitution and varying every material interaction dimension.

grounding.quote: | evaluation family | Do the actual participants at one declared material composition boundary satisfy their joint contract across the combinations of state, authority, configuration, timing, failure and recovery that can change the boundary result? |

value.label: Integration frame

conditions: Selected for one exact module-owned law and module-bounded population.
value.definition: Unit evaluation binds one exact module boundary, accepted ontology/design, active carrier inventory, module requirements/public contracts, implementation and a module-bounded decidable oracle. Its manifold includes public contracts, algebras/calculations, parsers/reducers/state machines/transitions/combinators, admission predicates, conservation/invariants, numerical boundaries and failures. Coordinates distinguish module/implementation revision, law/operator family, state/input/boundary class, expected relation/generated case/mutation/result. Evidence may include law-derived examples, equivalence classes, available finite exhaustion, property/generative cases, metamorphic relations, independent calculation/algebra oracles, boundary cases and killed internal mutations. The envelope requires independent oracle derivation and recognition of implementation restatement.

grounding.quote: | evaluation family | Does one module-owned law hold across its material combinations of algebraic operator, calculation regime, state, transition, public or private boundary class, and failure case? |

value.label: Unit frame

value.definition: Testing value is indexed first by material combinations discriminated for the exact claim. At least eight coordinates matter: claim/subject congruence; number/materiality of independent dimensions; covered interaction strength; authoritative-path exactness; oracle independence/precision; sensitivity to realistic faults/rivals/history; observability/reconstruction/reproducibility; residual combinations and invalidators. Unit value normally grows with module-internal combinatorial complexity. Broader value can be multiplicative through interactions, not mere interface visits. Common Product factors are role/capability, operation/composition, definition/owner/implementation/dependency, lifecycle/persisted state, configuration/version, process/continuation/retry/re-entry/recovery, success/refusal/malformed/partial-failure/rival cases, fresh-process/replay/reconstruction/migration, and visible outcome/projection.
value.label: Combinatorial testing-value index

value.definition: Technical-debt erasure evaluates two distinct finite subject-relative graphs: production closure, covering the exact runnable Product/configuration and transitive imports, exports, packages, switches, registries, fallbacks, consumers, generated runtime artifacts, recovery and fresh-process reconstruction; and assurance/source closure, covering relied-on source consumers, fixtures, proof scripts, generators, mutations and tooling. Success of a successor does not establish removal of its predecessor.

grounding.quote:
A successor passing does not prove the predecessor removed. Technical-debt
erasure evaluates two distinct, finite, subject-relative graphs

value.label: Production and assurance/source closure

value.definition: Evidence composition permits one execution to supply distinct bound results: user-outcome evidence, complete-path evidence, selected-seam evidence and module-law counterexamples. Each states its predicate and combines only through declared relations; a necessary-condition result is not the obligation, and conjunction sufficiency is itself a claim.

grounding.quote:
Each bound result states which
predicate it establishes; a result over a necessary condition does not
establish the obligation, and the sufficiency of a conjunction is a claim
of its own

value.label: Claim-bound evidence composition

value.definition: Assurance-subject acquisition and evaluation are distinct. Owner-issued Product/runtime/lifecycle/admission/replay/projection truth is acquired from the exact runnable owner surface, validator, projection, receipt or reconstruction relation; an independent Product/requirement/accepted-design oracle then evaluates it. Generic mechanics may calculate bytes, digests, order, equality, set membership, completeness and conjunction over owner-issued evidence without becoming domain owners.

grounding.quote:
Acquiring the assurance subject and evaluating it are distinct relations
(P6, P1; provenance #assurance-subject-acquisition-and-evaluation). Where a
claim depends on owner-issued Product, runtime, lifecycle, admission,
replay or projection truth, the testing frame acquires that truth through
the exact runnable owner surface, validator, projection, receipt or
reconstruction relation.

value.label: Owner-issued assurance subject

value.definition: Counterexample localisation returns the earliest supported causal frontier: causally minimal violated owner relations or seam coordinates under the declared causal relation, not earliest log/time position. Exactly one domain form accompanies its core result: unique violated locus → satisfied; jointly established incomparable earliest loci whose combined violation is necessary to the explanation → satisfied; unresolved alternative frontiers → indeterminate with alternatives; no supported bounded frontier → indeterminate with needed evidence. The predicate is that evidence establishes the counterexample's earliest violated loci on the declared path.

grounding.quote:
One unique violated locus and a jointly established set
map to `satisfied`. Unresolved alternative frontiers map to
`indeterminate`, naming the alternatives that further evidence must
decide between. The fourth form is the core value `indeterminate` itself,
naming the evidence a bounded frontier needs. The form travels with the
value as the domain outcome, so a joint set stays distinct from a unique
locus and unresolved alternatives stay distinct from an unbounded
frontier.

value.label: Counterexample localisation domain

conditions: Selected by the governing frame configuration or admitted work authority.
value.definition: urn:stdo:reference-frame:end-to-end-interface-integration:v1 is a composite refinement resolving in REFERENCE_FRAME's urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation under the exact selected basis, with assurance law here. It asks whether one outcome remains constructable, understandable and correctly realised across material interfaces with sufficient context and preserved meaning, authority and cause. It relates public boundaries, design, operators, owners and proof to existing integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance frames; it adds no fifth type, role or universal gate. It binds one outcome and independent oracle, requirements/design, exact checkpoint, contracts and finite cases; design claims use declared participants/paths/dependencies/configuration/capabilities, realised claims actual participants/callables/supported entry-exit/exact artifact or install. Coordinates distinguish Product/artifact/install/workspace/observation/invocation/candidate/admitted-result/evidence identities, revisions, domains, units, cardinality, order, empty/null/default meaning and validity interval.

grounding.quote:
Like the set, it is available and is
activated only where the governing frame configuration or admitted work
authority selects it. It adds no fifth testing type, role or
universal activation gate

value.label: End-to-end interface integration frame

value.definition: Four interface claims stay distinct: contract sufficiency asks whether each participant can determine/perform its responsibility from declared interface and available context, potentially established by design evidence without runtime; boundary congruence asks whether actual selected producers/transformations/consumers preserve domains, meaning, lifecycle and authority, requiring both sides and exchanges; path realisation asks whether the exact runnable subject follows the authoritative entry-to-outcome state/effect/observation path; user usability asks whether an ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtains the outcome with only declared context/access/supported surface.

grounding.quote: | user usability | Can the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtain the selected outcome using only its declared context, access and supported surface? Internal success or validator-aware fixtures cannot establish this claim. |

value.label: Four interface-integration claims

conditions: For each material seam in an activated interface evaluation.

Existing truth surfaces are reused. The working record adds only missing
cross-interface relations; schemas, prompts, adapters, indexes and tests do
not become another contract owner

grounding.quote:
The evaluation binds fact
establishment, each consumer, validity and invalidation, effects, retained
alternatives and accumulated work. It evaluates equivalent computation
across different domain names without assuming semantic equivalence.

value.label: Computational whole-path evaluation

value.definition: The subject's Tier-1 STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems, a_c, is a domain-specific, carrier-neutral constitutional calculus. Its stable concept identity is urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c, owned in urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus. It owns theory, signature, typed records, AC-001–AC-020, traversals, functor kinds, interpretation, models, layers, identity, application/import boundaries, exclusions and conformance obligations. Tier 1. Owns the a_c theory in full: position and scope, the signature,
the typed records, the laws AC-001 to AC-020, traversals and functor
kinds, interpretation and models, the three governed layers, the law of
calculus identity, the application boundary, external imports, exclusions
and the conformance obligations of this member.

Its stable
concept identity is `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c`. This member
owns that concept in the bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus`. Both identifiers are
declared identities and do not change with the carrier or the directory
that publishes them (P3; rc.2 #position).

value.label: Subject a_c calculus

value.definition: The derivation account links nine recurring commitments to current owners and rc.2 clause families: scoped identity/authority conservation (FOUNDATIONS §2; IDENTITY_METHOD core-law and UP-004); bounded-context meaning (FOUNDATIONS §2; SPEC_METHOD semantic resolution); bounded probabilistic construction (P0, FOUNDATIONS §2, ACTIVATION §1; REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD position/evaluation); delegated construction and assessment separation (ACTIVATION §1, EVALUATION §3; SPEC_METHOD UP-020); ambiguity and human adjudication/hard stops (ACTIVATION §4; SPEC_METHOD ambiguity governance); exact-basis/evidence-verdict separation and closed results (RF-005/006/007 and FOUNDATIONS §4 restating RF-012); constitutional derivation/re-entry (SPEC_METHOD §1/§4); finite closure/projection/residuals/capability fit (REFERENCE_FRAME §3, AC-010/011); singular released authority (SPEC_METHOD §6, PRODUCT_DEFINITION activation). These are provenance accounts, not imported normative definitions.

grounding.quote:
These references establish provenance. The definitions and laws of this
member are the sole normative authority for the meaning of `a_c` within
the selected complete cut. A consumer needs no implicit representation of
the method, no particular carrier and no downstream implementation to
interpret the calculus (P1, P6).

value.label: Calculus derivation account

value.definition: Material family F9's foundation-to-law table distinguishes premises, consequences, added choices and their owners. Its instance premises are finite model representation, separately identified exact subject/model/optional carrier, and mechanically decidable versus probabilistic or human predicates. P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 are marked independent; P0 recovered; P4b derived from P0/P2; P5 derived from P0/P6. The table maps these to position, scope, signature/reference closure, identity/typing, authority/basis, result/refusal, latitude, residuals, closure/projection, overlay, transformation, judgment separation, traversal/composition, interpretation/validity, layers, edition identity, application boundaries, constraint surfaces and conformance. Added choices remain owned: calculus names/core shapes/refusal precedence/canonicalisation/minimum conformance by this member; domains and contracts by signatures; latitude, overlays, transformations and composites by their named owners; semantic acceptance and downstream products by downstream authorities; task seeds/relations by activation.

grounding.quote:
Instance premises,
which the commitments do not supply:

- (i) a governed symbolic system is represented by a finite model whose
  records stand for its objects, relations, constraints, residuals,
  traversals, transformations and judgments;
- (ii) a model is interpreted from an exact subject and may be encoded in
  a carrier, and subject, model and carrier are separately identified;
- (iii) some predicates over a model are decided mechanically, and others
  need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication.

value.label: Foundation-to-law and consumer map

value.definition: M_b = (b,I,O,E,C,L,X,V,T,J): exact basis; closed identity universe; finite semantic-object, directed-relation, constraint, latitude, residual, traversal, transformation and judgment populations. Population_M maps each fixed record kind to its corresponding population. Local_M is their disjoint union; I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M. RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind,field) specifies cardinality, allowed local record kinds, semantic-object sorts, external target kinds and required basis relation.

grounding.quote:
`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population
is finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and
record identities are unique across their disjoint union.

value.label: Exact-basis model and populations

value.definition: SemanticObject has exactly id, sort, context, owner, scope, basis, value. Id, sort, context, owner and basis are identities; scope is the closed governed domain; value is sort-defined carrier-neutral content or an exact-content reference. Id, owner and sort carry scoped Object identity; scope carries its boundary.

grounding.quote:
`id`, `sort`, `context`, `owner` and `basis` are identities. `scope` is
the closed governed domain. `value` is sort-defined carrier-neutral content
or a reference to exact content. A semantic object is an Object of
FOUNDATIONS §2 whose scoped identity is carried by `id`, `owner` and
`sort` and whose boundary is `scope`.

value.label: SemanticObject record

value.definition: TypedRelation has exactly id, kind, source, target, context, owner, scope, basis, qualifiers. Endpoints resolve in I. Qualifiers are a closed kind-specific record of signature-required direction, cardinality, preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other relation semantics.

`source` and `target` resolve to members of `I`. `qualifiers` is the
closed kind-specific record declaring direction, cardinality,
preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other relation semantics
required by the signature.

value.label: TypedRelation record

value.definition: Constraint has exactly id, kind, applies_to, predicate, context, owner, scope, basis, judgment_kind, latitude_ref, refusal. Kind and judgment_kind resolve declared ConstraintKind and JudgmentKind identities. The signature owns predicate language and judgment semantics.

`kind` resolves one declared `ConstraintKind`; `judgment_kind` resolves
one declared `JudgmentKind`. The owning signature defines the predicate
language and how its result is judged.

value.label: Constraint record

value.definition: Latitude is an explicit permission set within a constraint boundary, with exactly id, applies_to, allowed_variation, forbidden_variation, context, owner, scope, basis, invalidation.

value.label: Latitude record

Its kind resolves one declared ResidualKind; the signature defines all lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation domains.

`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. The owning signature defines

value.definition: AC-001–AC-020 govern signature, typed and traversal records and the FOUNDATIONS ontology. Identity, authority, basis and residual definitions remain owned by FOUNDATIONS; the calculus owns these laws over them.

The objects these laws govern are the records of §2, §3 and §5 and the
ontology of FOUNDATIONS §2; where a law names identity, authority, basis
or residual, the definition is FOUNDATIONS' and the law is this member's.

value.label: Fundamental calculus laws

value.definition: Constraint judgments and calculus operation outcomes map to the existing core values satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, for their own named predicates. Operation stops include hold, gap, refusal(constraint) and refusal(basis); refusal causes are part of their values. Missing judgments and unapplied operations have no result.

grounding.quote:
This law applies them to the
judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
member, and adds no core value.

value.label: Core results and cause-specific stops

value.definition: For model M, seed Z and exact dependency relation family R, closure_R(M,Z) = lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M,Q)). This is least lawful record closure under R, not globally minimal prose, bytes, tokens, cost or cognitive effort.

grounding.quote: closure_R(M, Z) = lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M, Q))

value.label: Material closure

value.definition: Projection selects meaning-preserving model views: project(M,Z,R) returns (M_Z,Boundary_Z), gap or refusal. M_Z contains Z's material closure; Boundary_Z records excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. A projection is a reference, not a new semantic owner.

grounding.quote:
`M_Z` contains the material closure of `Z`, so a projection's `gap` or
`refusal` is that of the closure it contains or of the model it acts on:
`gap` or `refusal(basis)` (AC-007). `Boundary_Z` records excluded,
external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. A
projection is not a new semantic owner.

value.label: Model projection

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,

evaluation, verification, admission, execution, projection and retirement;
attribution from permission; and ownership of domain meaning from
ownership of runtime effects

value.definition: A complete transformation-admission relation determines durable entity truth over entity identity, predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision cardinality, admission predicate, durable result and supersession law. For every consequential entity-transition domain, design evidence contains
the complete transformation-admission relation over entity identity,
predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision
cardinality, admission predicate, resulting durable fact and supersession
law, through the authority matrix or an equivalent closed representation
(P6, P4b):

value.label: Complete transformation-admission relation

value.definition: The DESIGN_MODULE profile describes Ontology-first engineering design and preferred realisation structure inside implementation and design modules, with explicit authority, effects, low coupling and semantic non-bleed. grounding.quote:
this profile what is
the preferred implementation design discipline

value.label: Design-module profile

value.definition: The Ontology is one semantic truth. Diagrams, matrices, IACS, public interfaces, schemas, architecture, modules, implementation and proof inventories preserve that truth as projections; their presence does not make them independent semantic authorities.

grounding.quote:
The Ontology is one semantic truth (P1, P6; rc.2 #ontology-projection-law).
These preserve it and do not become independent semantic authorities:

value.label: Ontology

value.definition: An atomic function family is a parameterised semantic operation derived from the Ontology to make entity lifecycles logically complete. grounding.quote: | Discovered functionality | Entity | Atomic function or template | Higher-order composition | Effect class | Required authority | Disposition |

value.label: Atomic function family

value.definition: Higher-order composition is governed by an explicit composition and effect algebra. Typical categories are unit or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and projection.

grounding.quote:
Typical categories include unit
or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold
or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and
projection.

value.label: Higher-order composition

value.definition: A Prime semantic atom is an irreducible design relation: an atomic function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot honestly be composed from other accepted atoms with the same meaning. Prime is decided at semantic-design altitude.

grounding.quote:
A Prime semantic atom is one irreducible design relation: an atomic
function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation,
topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot be expressed
honestly by composing other accepted atoms while preserving the same
meaning

value.label: Prime semantic atom

value.definition: Whole-family Prime contraction reviews the entire candidate semantic-atom family and every proposed realisation projection. Prime review evaluates the complete candidate semantic-atom family and
every proposed realisation projection, not only functions, carriers or
each atom in isolation.

value.definition: Realisation projections include functions, classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules. A unit can implement several atoms and an atom can project into several units; physical size, separate naming, typing and independent testability do not establish Prime.

One atom may project into several realisation
units, and one realisation unit may implement several atoms, provided the
mapping is explicit and introduces no rival meaning or authority.

value.definition: The Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set, IACS, is the smallest lawful top-level carrier family needed for a boundary's real functionality and authority flow. Example roles are source truth, admission, execution, yielded or recovery, effect plan and public projection carriers.

grounding.quote:
The IACS is the smallest
set of carriers required to carry the real functionality and authority
flow of the boundary.

value.label: Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set

  is not top-level by default;

  promoted into extra peer types without irreducible need.

value.definition: The three-view design asset contains a structural domain classDiagram, behavioural execution sequenceDiagram and lifecycle stateDiagram-v2. value.label: Three-view design asset

grounding.quote:
the selected method describes which relations
are required and how to reason about them; the accepted design supplies
the concrete invariant values.

value.label: Invariant reconstruction and action decisions

on the exact
Ontology and design basis, the boundary's design meets the axiom, or the
axiom does not apply to the boundary

The Ontology verdict and the design verdict are each an acceptance
result: a decision that consumes the results of assessment, distinct from
them.

value.label: Ontology and design acceptance

value.definition: The subordinate computational realisation projection exposes abstract data types, identity/key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation/effect boundaries, selected implementations and domain-to-computational mappings. the design projects the
domain design into its computational realisation: abstract data types,
identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and
effect boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational
mappings.

grounding.quote:
modules should be
classified by role (P0, P6; rc.2 #6-design-module-taxonomy). Recommended

semantic function returns are the Product's domain values, not results of
this method; an evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value

value.label: Product outcomes and method results

value.definition: Governance surfaces describe state, boundary and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor should work. grounding.quote:
Governance surfaces describe the state, boundary
and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor
should do the work.

value.label: Governance and strategy surfaces

value.definition: A recurring realisation pattern across more than one processed boundary is a commonisation candidate. The complete selected function is the causal closure of the declared
claim, not the whole Product or the whole history of its construction.

When a project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable

value.definition: Product family: evaluates whether one exact current Product claim, outcome, boundary and lifecycle govern the subject without downstream reinterpretation, using current Intent, Product, requirements, acceptance meaning and exact coordinates. Product and requirement authority retain meaning and acceptance; output is bounded evaluation and evidence only. Immediate falsifier: design, code, tests, predecessor behaviour or local convention changes Product meaning or substitutes another Product subject.

grounding.quote: Product and requirement authority keep meaning and acceptance. The frame returns only a bounded evaluation result and evidence.

value.label: Product evaluation family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Product Composition family: evaluates an exact directed Product relation preserving source/target roles, Product Definition, Release Cut, Product and Install identities, Development Product role bindings, contracts, authority, lifecycle, evidence boundary and invalidation law. A chain uses bounded edge activations and declared conjunction. Each Product retains meaning; cited authority/contracts own the edge; output is evaluation evidence only. Falsifiers include connectivity or builder convenience creating/changing composition, confusing builder with authored Product, or one node silently redefining another.

grounding.quote: A chain is evaluated through bounded edge activations and a declared conjunction.

value.label: Product Composition family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Design family: evaluates whether accepted structural HOW satisfies material constitutional WHAT, closes required design relations and preserves owners across affected topology. Accepted design under Product and requirements owns structure; output may identify satisfaction, contradiction or design re-entry gap, never invent Product truth. Falsifiers: implementation precedent resolves open material design decisions, design creates Product meaning, or material relations/competing structures remain undeclared.

grounding.quote: The frame may identify satisfaction, contradiction or a design re-entry gap; it cannot invent Product truth.

value.label: Design family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Design Component family: evaluates one bounded component and direct causal dependency cone against parent contract, internal relations, sibling seams and required outputs. Accepted design owns only its bounded composition decision; parent, sibling, Product, requirement and runtime owners retain theirs. Falsifiers: omitted material far-side seam, absorbed sibling/parent decision, or local closure with unresolved direct composition.

grounding.quote: The accepted design boundary owns only its bounded composition decision. Parent, sibling, Product, requirement and runtime owners keep their relations.

value.label: Design Component family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Public Boundary family: evaluates a supported public entry/exit's assigned validation, selection, transport, refusal and projection while preserving interior owners. Product, interface, identity, security and accepted design define the boundary. Output is closed boundary evaluation or refusal, without recreating interior semantics. Falsifiers: interpreting owner meaning, sequencing hidden domain decisions, presenting interior carriers as Product truth, or admitting unsupported paths.

grounding.quote: The frame evaluates the boundary result or refusal and returns only its closed evaluation; it does not recreate interior semantics.

value.label: Public Boundary family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Entity family: evaluates a semantic, artifact or runtime entity's exact identity, kind, lifecycle, owner, representation and applicable effect regime under Product, domain, identity, requirement and accepted-design authority. Output is identity- and lifecycle-bound evaluation. Falsifiers: filename, wrapper, ticket, object shape, cache or process substitutes for stable identity, or distinct lifecycle coordinates collapse.

grounding.quote: The frame returns an identity- and lifecycle-bound evaluation.

value.label: Entity family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Operator family: evaluates a material operation as an irreducible declared relation over admitted domain, inputs, outputs, refusals, algebra, effects and lawful compositions. Product, requirements, accepted ontology/design and named operation owner define it; evaluation creates no additional executable plan. Falsifiers: implementation label asserted as semantic atom, orchestration hiding the operator, or generic mechanics rebuilt as domain law.

grounding.quote: The frame evaluates it without creating another executable plan.

value.label: Operator family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Owner family: evaluates preservation of a semantic/authority relation's owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis, lifecycle, refusal invariants and permitted delegation. The existing named authority owns the relation; this frame only evaluates authority congruence. Falsifiers: another surface recreates judgment, authorship implies authority transfer, or proxy, foundation, frame or actor widens a grant.

grounding.quote: The frame may evaluate authority congruence only.

value.label: Owner family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Effect family: evaluates an action's pure, observational, artifact or runtime effect regime, including material commit, failure, retry, recovery, compensation, admission and projection law. Applicable Product, requirement, design, artifact, runtime and admission owners retain decisions; output is effect-bound result/evidence. Falsifiers: collapsed regimes, mutation bypassing owner, compensation treated as semantic rollback, or a read becoming rival writable truth.

grounding.quote: The frame returns an effect-bound result and evidence.

value.label: Effect family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Reuse/Foundation family: evaluates normalisation and comparison of a material generic capability/dependency against credible lawful foundations, preserving irreducible local remainder and authority-bearing role. Design-profile selection law and existing trade-off owner govern; semantic authority cannot move to a foundation. Falsifiers: incumbent/local code wins without bounded comparison, richer lawful foundation is reproduced, unknowns receive favourable scores, or reuse acquires owner authority.

grounding.quote: The frame cannot move semantic authority to a foundation.

value.label: Reuse/Foundation family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Install family: evaluates exact Product, release, artifact, dependency set, configuration and callable entry through admitted installed coordinates, independent of mutable source convenience. Product, identity, release, dependency, packaging and accepted design define the subject; output is installed identity, reachability and refusal evidence. Falsifiers: source imports, ambient resolution, registries, fixtures, rebuilt artifacts or moving workspace replace the claimed installed subject.

grounding.quote: The frame returns installed identity, reachability and refusal evidence.

value.label: Install family

conditions: Resolved in the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context.
value.definition: Proof family: evaluates one exact claim's congruent subject, basis, path, population, oracle, evidence, falsifier, residual boundary and invalidation law. Claim owner defines meaning; testing, assurance, review, Product and release owners define evaluation/acceptance. Output is evidence and closed evaluation, never Product meaning or disposition. Falsifiers: harness recreates meaning, evidence targets another subject/path, count or aggregate green replaces claim, or proof tooling mutates subject undetectably.

grounding.quote: The frame returns evidence and a closed evaluation result, not Product meaning or disposition.

value.label: Proof family

value.definition: FOUNDATIONS is a Tier 1 member owning standing vocabulary; ontology and imports; commitments P0–P6, foundation-to-law format and material-family index; composition, conservation, core results, conjunction and categorical demonstration requirements; and hypotheses.
